Topics · One God, one message

What does it mean to make your desire your god?

A person can have a god they never named. The Quran asks and accuses no one. Read your choices from last week.

Part 1 of 3

﴿أَرَءَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him?

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:43

Translation

whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who think about earthly things.

Original · Ancient Greek

ὧν τὸ τέλος ἀπώλεια, ὧν ὁ θεὸς ἡ κοιλία καὶ ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ αὐτῶν, οἱ τὰ ἐπίγεια φρονοῦντες.

Philippians · 3:19

World English Bible

What makes something a god in a person's life? Not what they say, but what they finally defer to when things collide. If the last word in your life is what you want right now, then that is doing the work of a god, whatever you call it. The verse asks in one word: have you seen? It rules on no one. It asks you to recognise the shape when you meet it.

A question for you

What has the last word in your life when things collide?

Part 2 of 3

﴿أَفَرَءَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمْعِهِۦ وَقَلْبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَـٰوَةً فَمَن يَهْدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and Allāh has sent him astray due to knowledge[1473] and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allāh? Then will you not be reminded?

Translator's notes

[1473] This can refer to Allāh's knowledge of that person and of his preference for his own inclinations or to that person's knowledge of the truth while he refuses it.

Quran · Al-Jathiyah 45:23

Translation

Don’t go after your lusts. Restrain your appetites. If you give fully to your soul the delight of her desire, she will make you the laughing stock of your enemies. Don’t make merry in much luxury, and don’t be tied to its expense.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ὀπίσω τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν σου μὴ πορεύου, καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀρέξεών σου κωλύου. Ἐὰν χορηγήσεῃς τῇ ψυχῇ σου εὐδοκίαν ἐπιθυμίας, ποιήσει σε ἐπίχαρμα τῶν ἐχθρῶν σου. Μὴ εὐφραίνου ἐπὶ πολλῇ τρυφῇ, μηδὲ προσδεθῇς συμβολῇ αὐτῆς.

Sirach · 18:30-32

World English Bible

This verse connects with what came earlier in the chapter. Six verses back, 45:17 said people differed after knowledge came to them, out of rivalry. Now it speaks of one who takes desire as a god and adds "upon knowledge", which some commentators read as: even though he knows. That answers an old puzzle: how can someone who knows divide people? Because knowledge is not enough when desire is in charge. Desire uses knowledge; it goes looking for the argument after the decision is made.

A question for you

What does desire do to knowledge, as you see it?

If you sayMakes it a tool
ThenThen knowledge does not protect the one who has it. That makes this mirror one for every learned person before anyone else.
If you sayCovers it over
ThenThat is near the verse's own picture: a veil on the sight. What is covered still exists, and can be uncovered.
If you sayHas no power over it
ThenIf so, knowledge alone would unite people. What do you make of what you see among the learned?

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ وَنَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ٤٠ فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ٤١﴾

Translation of the meaning

But as for he who feared the position of his Lord[1847] and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination, Then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.

Translator's notes

[1847] See footnote to 55:46.

Quran · An-Nazi'at 79:40-41

Translation

But each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own lust and enticed. Then the lust, when it has conceived, bears sin. The sin, when it is full grown, produces death.

Original · Ancient Greek

ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος· εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν, ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον.

James · 1:14-15

World English Bible

﴿يَـٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَـٰكَ خَلِيفَةً فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌۢ بِمَا نَسُوا۟ يَوْمَ ٱلْحِسَابِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[We said], "O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire, as it will lead you astray from the way of Allāh." Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allāh will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account.

Quran · Sad 38:26

Translation

David reigned over all Israel; and David executed justice and righteousness for all his people.

Original · Hebrew

וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ דָּוִ֖ד עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י דָוִ֗ד עֹשֶׂ֛ה מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה לְכָל־עַמּֽוֹ׃

2 Samuel · 8:15

World English Bible

If desire were the whole story, this would be a story without hope. But the first verse shows another person: one who held the self back from desire, and the Garden is their home. Desire can be told no. The second speaks to David, king and prophet: do not follow desire. If this was said even to a prophet, then the pull is no disgrace and no proof you are ruined. It is every person's condition. The way is to know it and turn back.

A question for you

What does it mean to you that this was said to a prophet?

If you sayI am not alone in this
ThenYou are not. That brings the return closer than it seems.
If you sayNo one is above account
ThenThat includes every teacher and leader, and a question ahead asks whether obeying a person can be a kind of worship.
If you sayI still do not know what my desire is
ThenThat takes time. The next question starts there: how do I know my opinions aren't my ego?

The same in the other books

Translation

Put to death therefore your members which are on the earth: sexual immorality, uncleanness, depraved passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry.

Original · Ancient Greek

Νεκρώσατε οὖν τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, πορνείαν, ἀκαθαρσίαν, πάθος, ἐπιθυμίαν κακήν, καὶ τὴν πλεονεξίαν ἥτις ἐστὶν εἰδωλολατρία,

Colossians · 3:5

World English Bible

Translation

God, give the king your justice; your righteousness to the royal son. He will judge your people with righteousness, and your poor with justice. The mountains shall bring prosperity to the people. The hills bring the fruit of righteousness. He will judge the poor of the people. He will save the children of the needy, and will break the oppressor in pieces.

Original · Hebrew

לִשְׁלֹמֹ֨ה ׀ אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים מִ֭שְׁפָּטֶיךָ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ תֵּ֑ן וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ לְבֶן־מֶֽלֶךְ׃ יָדִ֣ין עַמְּךָ֣ בְצֶ֑דֶק וַעֲנִיֶּ֥יךָ בְמִשְׁפָּֽט׃ יִשְׂא֤וּ הָרִ֓ים שָׁ֘ל֥וֹם לָעָ֑ם וּ֝גְבָע֗וֹת בִּצְדָקָֽה׃ יִשְׁפֹּ֤ט ׀ עֲֽנִיֵּי־עָ֗ם י֭וֹשִׁיעַ לִבְנֵ֣י אֶבְי֑וֹן וִֽידַכֵּ֣א עוֹשֵֽׁק׃

the Psalms · 72:1-4

World English Bible

He who knows other men is discerning; he who knows himself is intelligent. He who overcomes others is strong; he who overcomes himself is mighty. He who is satisfied with his lot is rich; he who goes on acting with energy has a (firm) will.

Chinese classics · Tao Te Ching 33.1

Tao Teh King (Legge)

Translation

“Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their heart, and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. Should I be inquired of at all by them?

Original · Hebrew

בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הֶעֱל֤וּ גִלּֽוּלֵיהֶם֙ עַל־לִבָּ֔ם וּמִכְשׁ֣וֹל עֲוֺנָ֔ם נָתְנ֖וּ נֹ֣כַח פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם הַאִדָּרֹ֥שׁ אִדָּרֵ֖שׁ לָהֶֽם׃
